prompt: Which packaging and update stack may the implementation prototype use?
recommendationReason: MSIX/App Installer and Velopack both require isolated evidence before committing the product and supply chain.

options.label: Prototype both
options.impact: Allows non-production comparison without choosing the production stack.

options.label: MSIX/App Installer
options.impact: Commits the prototype to Windows package identity and App Installer behavior.

options.label: Velopack
options.impact: Introduces a third-party desktop update tool into the prototype supply chain.

options.label: ClickOnce
options.impact: Uses the simpler .NET deployment route with reduced channel and rollback flexibility.

options.label: Decide later
options.impact: Blocks implementation of the packaging/update stack.

prompt: Which hosting and budget boundary may serve immutable update artifacts and channel manifests?
recommendationReason: Hosting creates recurring cost, production infrastructure, access logs, availability commitments, and privileged credentials.

options.label: GitHub Releases
options.impact: Uses GitHub availability and access-log boundaries with limited channel control.

options.label: Object storage/CDN
options.impact: Adds cloud cost and operations but supports immutable paths and controlled promotion.

options.label: Owner-hosted static
options.impact: Places TLS, uptime, logs, capacity, and incident response on Owner-managed infrastructure.

options.label: Decide later
options.impact: Blocks external hosting and production update endpoints.

prompt: Which Windows code-signing certificate identity, certificate class, supplier, cost, and renewal policy may D4Hub use?
recommendationReason: Certificate procurement changes cost, legal identity, player trust, SmartScreen expectations, and renewal risk.

options.label: Standard organization certificate
options.impact: Uses an organization identity with supplier cost and reputation-building requirements.

options.label: EV/managed signing
options.impact: Raises cost and operational constraints in exchange for stronger custody and reputation options.

options.label: Eligible individual option
options.impact: Depends on supplier and jurisdiction eligibility and exposes the selected legal identity.

options.label: Decide later
options.impact: Blocks certificate purchase and real signing.

prompt: Which private-key custody, CI identity, release approval, rotation, and emergency revocation model may be used?
recommendationReason: Exportable long-lived keys in ordinary CI secrets create unacceptable fleet-wide compromise risk.

options.label: Managed signing + OIDC + two-person approval
options.impact: Uses short-lived CI identity, non-exportable keys, and separate release approval.

options.label: Hardware token offline release
options.impact: Keeps keys off CI but makes releases more manual and device-dependent.

options.label: Self-managed HSM
options.impact: Provides strong custody with greater infrastructure and operational cost.

options.label: Decide later
options.impact: Blocks production signing configuration.

prompt: Which .NET runtime packaging policy may be used for player installers?
recommendationReason: The choice affects installer size, patch bandwidth, runtime prerequisites, support, and vulnerability servicing.

options.label: Self-contained x64
options.impact: Simplifies first install but increases artifact and update size.

options.label: Framework-dependent x64
options.impact: Reduces application size but requires Desktop Runtime detection and support.

options.label: Offer both
options.impact: Increases release matrix, documentation, storage, and validation cost.

options.label: Decide later
options.impact: Blocks production package format finalization.

prompt: Which minimum Windows version, architecture set, and support lifetime may the public release promise?
recommendationReason: The current README statement is not a lifecycle-backed public support commitment and Windows 10 support varies by edition and program.

options.label: Windows 11 x64
options.impact: Narrows support and testing to the current Windows client generation.

options.label: Supported Windows 10 + 11 x64
options.impact: Broadens reach but requires an explicit Windows 10 servicing eligibility rule and larger test matrix.

options.label: Decide later
options.impact: Blocks the public minimum-system promise.

prompt: Which telemetry and crash-reporting boundary may D4Hub adopt?
recommendationReason: Data collection and third-party processing require explicit purpose, consent, retention, access, deletion, and vendor decisions.

options.label: Local diagnostics only
options.impact: Keeps automatic telemetry and crash uploads disabled; players export a redacted bundle manually.

options.label: Separate opt-in crash reports
options.impact: Adds a crash processor and consent flow without usage analytics.

options.label: Separate opt-in minimal telemetry
options.impact: Adds approved event schemas, consent, retention, deletion, and processor governance.

options.label: Decide later
options.impact: Keeps automatic collection blocked.

prompt: Which update channels, rollout grouping, stop thresholds, and device-identifier policy may be used?
recommendationReason: Random device cohorts can create persistent identifiers and every rollout policy creates player-impact and incident obligations.

options.label: Explicit preview then stable
options.impact: Uses opt-in preview players and manual channel promotion without permanent device IDs.

options.label: Signed random cohorts
options.impact: Adds cohort logic and a separately governed identifier/privacy design.

options.label: Stable only
options.impact: Simplifies channels but reduces pre-release player evidence and increases blast radius.

options.label: Decide later
options.impact: Blocks production rollout policy.

prompt: Which supported-version window, incident response target, final artifact retention, and service exit commitment may be promised?
recommendationReason: Support and end-of-life promises create ongoing cost and player rights that must be explicitly owned.

options.label: Current + previous stable
options.impact: Keeps a bounded recovery window but requires two-version incident and compatibility support.

options.label: Current stable only
options.impact: Reduces maintenance but increases forced-upgrade and rollback pressure.

options.label: Fixed time window
options.impact: Requires Owner to set and fund a concrete support duration and response target.

options.label: Decide later
options.impact: Blocks public support and EOL commitments.

prompt: Does the Owner authorize a specific production signing, upload, public release, or real-player distribution now?
recommendationReason: This governance phase explicitly excludes signing and release; future production authorization must bind a version, digest, channel, rollout, and stop conditions.

options.label: Approve
options.impact: Only valid in a later digest-bound Owner decision naming the exact release candidate and conditions.

options.label: Revise
options.impact: Returns the production proposal for changes without authorizing release.

options.label: Decide later
options.impact: Keeps signing, upload, public release, and player distribution blocked.
